evidence.quote: Were you approached by community and/or political party representatives?

claims.text: Interviewer-reported approach of the field team by community or party actors describes gatekeeping around access to the interview; it is not the respondent's own partisan affiliation and does not identify who approached whom.

evidence.quote: Did you feel threatened during the interview?

claims.text: Felt threat is the interviewer's subjective experience inside one encounter, so a positive report need not entail any bodily contact and cannot stand in for respondent-side danger.

evidence.quote: Were you physically threatened during the interview?

claims.text: Physical threat narrows felt threat to bodily intimidation, so the two items make distinguishable claims about the same interview and should not be collapsed into one safety indicator.
Candour is an interviewer's global attribution of respondent demeanour, not a verified truthfulness score; it can absorb language, comprehension and social-distance effects from the same encounter.

evidence.quote: must always obey the laws and the courts

claims.text: The forced choice opposes presidential exemption from law and courts to obligatory obedience, yielding an asserted constitutional stance about an abstract president rather than a verdict on any named ruling.

This general norm against military involvement in politics is conditionally paired with legitimate takeover amid abuse; it remains a principle-level endorsement rather than a judgment about a specific coup.
Oversight of MPs is posed as normative allocation among president, parliament or council, party, voters and no one, recording who ought to be accountable rather than whether any overseer acted.
The presidential counterpart reuses the same fixed option set as the MP item, so any MP-versus-president difference is measurable only within those offered categories and not through an open other.

evidence.quote: she will be criticized, called names, or harassed

claims.text: The respondent rates the likelihood of community harassment of a hypothetical woman candidate, an anticipated social reaction that does not report witnessed or experienced harassment.

evidence.quote: should government and elected officials be doing more

claims.text: The item asks for a desired direction and amount of state effort relative to current action, so assent to more effort is an evaluative demand rather than evidence that current effort is deficient in fact.

evidence.quote: most important for our government and society to address

claims.text: The stem frames a single top-priority choice among listed rights concerns, so the field records a capped ranking and not support or salience for each concern separately.

evidence.quote: using the police and security forces to enforce public health mandates

claims.text: Justification is conditional on a health emergency and about a possible measure, so agreement endorses a hypothetical policing power rather than describing enforcement that occurred.

evidence.quote: Who do you think sent us to do this interview?

claims.text: This records the respondent's belief about survey sponsorship, with party, government, research company, God and other as distinct options; misattribution is possible and it is not an audit of the actual commissioning body.

evidence.quote: Willing to participate in follow-up surveys

claims.text: Follow-up willingness carries a separate not-applicable code for respondents without a mobile number, so the field cannot be read as simple refusal versus consent across all respondents.

nominations.reason: Retrieving Q111 would allow interviewer-side reports in Q106C, Q106D, Q106E and Q109F to be grouped by fieldworker, distinguishing interviewer composition from encounter-level variation.

holds.missing: No interviewer identifier or visit-level record among the selected fields; interviewer attributes appear only as locator candidates such as Q111 to Q113.
holds.why: Threat and candour reports cannot be attributed to particular interviewers or separated from interviewer composition effects on the cited fields alone.

holds.missing: No wave, country or date field among the selected items, and bracketed office and place names remain unresolved placeholders.
holds.why: The constitutional referents and the emergency or gender module context cannot be fixed, so cross-national and across-time comparability of these normative items stays undetermined.

holds.missing: No routing or skip documentation showing whether the gender-module items were asked of all respondents and whether Q51B was conditioned on any prior answer.
holds.why: Whether the priority choice is an unconditioned response or a routed subsample cannot be established.

holds.missing: No administrative record of the true commissioning body and no record of later recontact attempts among the selected fields.
holds.why: Observed sponsor attribution cannot be validated against actual sponsorship, and stated follow-up willingness cannot be checked against later participation.
